Threat: Attacker controls SQL via unsanitised input
Mitigation: Use parameterised queries / prepared statements; ORM/query-builder; allow-list dynamic identifiers
Do: Bind parameters; validate identifiers from allow-list
Keywords: sqli sql injection prepared statement parameterised

Threat: Attacker injects script that runs in victim's browser
Mitigation: Context-aware output encoding; strict CSP; framework auto-escaping
Do: Escape per context (HTML/JS/CSS/URL); ship strict CSP with nonces
Don't: Render raw user input; use 'innerHTML' / 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML' on user data
Keywords: xss cross site scripting csp domsanitize

Threat: Browser is tricked into sending state-changing request to authenticated origin
Mitigation: Double-submit cookie or synchroniser token; SameSite=Lax/Strict cookies; origin/referer check
Do: Use anti-CSRF token on all state-changing endpoints; SameSite cookies
Don't: Rely solely on cookies for auth without anti-CSRF

Threat: Server is coerced to make a request the attacker can't (cloud metadata, internal LAN)
Mitigation: Allow-list outbound destinations; block link-local (169.254.169.254 / fd00::/8); use IMDSv2; egress proxy
Do: Resolve & validate hostnames before connect; pin to known prefixes
Don't: Pass user URLs straight to HTTP client
Tooling: aws imdsv2, smokescreen, codeql ssrf rules

Mitigation: Avoid native serializers (Java/Python pickle); use schema-bound formats (JSON+schema, Protobuf, Avro)
Do: Use safe formats with schema validation

Threat: Long-lived credential leaked via Git push
Mitigation: Pre-commit secret scanning; GitHub secret scanning; rotate on leak; use vault/secret manager
Do: Inject secrets at runtime from KMS/Vault

Mitigation: Continuous dependency scanning + auto PRs; SBOM publishing; pin versions
Do: Dependabot/Renovate auto PRs; review CVEs weekly; fail builds on critical
Don't: Pin and forget; ignore Dependabot alerts
Tooling: Dependabot, Renovate, Snyk, OSV-Scanner, Grype, Trivy
Keywords: cve sbom dependabot renovate trivy osv

Mitigation: Use distroless/chainguard base; scan in CI; rebuild weekly
Do: Pin digest, not 'latest'; sign images (Sigstore/cosign); SBOM in registry
Don't: Use 'latest' tags; long-lived AMIs without rebuild
Keywords: trivy grype cosign sigstore distroless chainguard

Threat: Build pipeline tampered, malicious source replaced
Mitigation: Sign commits; reproducible builds; SLSA L3+ provenance; verify at deploy
Do: Cosign-sign artefacts; verify signatures in admission controller
Don't: Pull binaries from random URLs without verification

Mitigation: mTLS everywhere; identity-based access; short-lived workload credentials; no flat L3
Do: SPIFFE/SPIRE identities; mesh mTLS; device posture for users
Tooling: spiffe spire, beyondcorp, tailscale, cloudflare access

Mitigation: Cloud-managed KMS encryption (default-on); envelope encryption for app data; rotate keys
Do: Use cloud KMS / HSM; per-tenant DEKs for B2B SaaS
Don't: Hand-roll crypto; store keys next to data
Tooling: aws kms, gcp kms, azure key vault, hashicorp vault

Mitigation: TLS 1.2+ only (1.3 preferred); disable weak ciphers; ALPN; OCSP stapling
Don't: Self-signed in prod; expired certs; downgrade attacks

Mitigation: Structured logging; allow-list fields; mask card/email/SSN; redact PII at the SDK level
Do: Use a redaction library; centralise logger config

Mitigation: Per-IP + per-account token bucket; CAPTCHAs on suspicious flows; WAF rules
Do: Lock accounts on abuse; add bot detection
Don't: Rely on infra rate-limit alone for app abuse
Tooling: cloudflare, aws waf, kong, envoy ratelimit
Keywords: rate limit waf brute force captcha

Threat: '*' or reflected origin allows credentialed cross-site reads
Mitigation: Allow-list explicit origins; never '*' with 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true'
Do: Use a reviewed CORS middleware; audit prod headers

Threat: Unknown OSS licences / vulnerable transitive deps in shipped artefacts
Mitigation: Generate SBOM at build (CycloneDX/SPDX); scan licences in CI
Do: Publish SBOM with releases; track AGPL / GPL boundaries

Mitigation: SAST in CI on every PR with a high-signal ruleset
Do: Use Semgrep + CodeQL with curated rulesets; gate on Critical findings
Don't: Drown in noise from default rulesets

Mitigation: Run DAST (ZAP/Burp) and fuzzers (libFuzzer/AFL/Atheris/Jazzer) in CI
Do: Continuous fuzzing on parsers; nightly DAST in staging
Don't: Fuzz only on a developer laptop
Tooling: OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, ClusterFuzzLite, OSS-Fuzz
Keywords: dast fuzzing zap burp clusterfuzz oss-fuzz
